criteria.justification: The response explicitly reframes the issue as “how to make a naming decision that stays made” and concludes that the failures were “one bad process applied three times,” directly identifying non-convergence as the core problem.

It proposes a single decision owner, pre-agreed acceptance criteria, a tie-breaking default, a decision record, and a reopening rule limited to new evidence of material customer harm. It also identifies ongoing costs such as review time, customer confusion, and loss of team credibility.

The response treats the prior tone, glossary, and technical-accuracy objections as substantively different, while drawing a boundary against reopening based merely on “preference or new reviewer.” This preserves room for genuinely new evidence without treating every later objection as equally dispositive.

It repeatedly treats the API field as a hard constraint, requiring the customer-facing term to “map to the locked API field” and suggesting a human-readable form rather than any architectural or field-name change.

Rather than simply proposing a fourth ad hoc name, it changes the process by fixing criteria and decision rights before candidates are shown, then comparing a small set head-to-head under one study. It explicitly contrasts this with repeating the prior loop, which it calls “near-certain to fail the same way.”
